[1] The patient presented with septic shock, cardiogenic shock, diarrhea, and abnormal coagulation profile.
[2] The primary diagnosis was septicemia due to escherichia coli [E. coli].
[3] Active diagnoses included septicemia due to escherichia coli [E. coli], acute respiratory failure, acute kidney failure, unspecified, chronic systolic heart failure, other primary cardiomyopathies, hyperosmolality and/or hypernatremia, pyelonephritis, unspecified, severe sepsis, congestive heart failure, unspecified, atrial fibrillation, secondary thrombocytopenia, anemia of other chronic disease, unspecified late effects of cerebrovascular disease, anisocoria, coronary atherosclerosis of native coronary artery, unspecified acquired hypothyroidism, and depressive disorder, not elsewhere classified.
[4] Past medical history included long-term (current) use of anticoagulants, heart valve replaced by other means, automatic implantable cardiac defibrillator in situ, and presence of cerebrospinal fluid drainage device.
[5] Procedures performed included continuous invasive mechanical ventilation for 96 consecutive hours or more, insertion of endotracheal tube, venous catheterization, arterial catheterization, enteral infusion of concentrated nutritional substances, and transfusion of packed cells.

[7] Microbiology results were negative.
[8] Services provided included Medicine and Medical Intensive Care Unit (MICU).
[9] The patient was discharged alive to HOME HEALTH CARE.
